notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When retrieving cryptographic keys from a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint, PyJWKClient fails to validate HTTP redirect destinations against trusted domain boundaries. A remote attacker who can influence the response of a trusted endpoint can redirect key requests to an untrusted server, allowing the client to accept forged verification keys or potentially exposing sensitive credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because improper handling of HTTP redirects during dynamic key retrieval can allow an adversary to supply forged cryptographic keys or intercept sensitive request headers. In Red Hat environments where services utilize PyJWKClient to fetch JSON Web Key Sets over the network, accepting untrusted key material may compromise token validation and authentication boundaries. Exploitation requires the target service to dynamically resolve keys via HTTP and relies on an attacker's ability to manipulate responses returned by the configured key server.

Consequently, the library improperly treats the public key as a shared secret key, allowing a remote attacker to forge valid authentication tokens and bypass security controls.

Exploitation occurs when consuming applications configure token verification to accept both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms simultaneously, allowing an asymmetric public key to be mishandled as a symmetric secret. Deployments that strictly enforce a single algorithm type or validate tokens using JSON Web Key sets do not permit this algorithm confusion and remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. When verifying cryptographic keys, the raw JSON Web Key (JWK) parser fails to normalize Unicode byte-order marks (BOM). In mixed-algorithm verification environments, an attacker who knows the public key can supply a key prefixed with a byte-order mark, causing the system to misidentify the public key as a shared symmetric secret. This flaw allows an attacker to forge authenticated JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and bypass authentication controls.

In Red Hat environments, exposure is restricted to services that simultaneously allow both symmetric HMAC and asymmetric signature algorithms while parsing public keys that contain byte order marks. Workloads and services that enforce single-algorithm verification policies or utilize standard asymmetric key validation routines are not susceptible to this attack.

This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass token validation checks when an application reuses an options configuration across multiple token decoding requests. notes.text: A flaw was found in multidict. The multidict C extension fails to release object references during certain items-view union and subtraction operations. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted input sequences to applications performing these operations, triggering uncollectable memory leaks. This issue can cause unbounded process memory growth, ultimately leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: multidict: multidict: Denial of Service via memory leak in items-view operations
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat products because triggering the memory leak requires an application to evaluate specific items-view set operations against untrusted user input, which is uncommon across standard deployments. While multiple Red Hat services bundle multidict, exploitation is limited to gradual memory exhaustion and denial of service, with no possibility of remote code execution or data disclosure. Furthermore, standard dictionary access patterns, forward unions, and intersections are not susceptible to this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in hydra-core. Target execution policies used during object instantiation are stored in mutable module-level state. An attacker who supplies crafted configuration entries can manipulate this policy to remove restrictions on blocked targets. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the permissions of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: hydra-core: hydra-core: Arbitrary code execution via mutable execution policy manipulation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in hydra-core, which is bundled in Red Hat AI Inference Server 3.3 and 3.4 and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI 3.4 container images. Hydra stores the target execution policies used during object instantiation in mutable module-level state. An attacker who can supply crafted configuration containing multiple sibling _target_ entries can resolve a mutation method on Hydra's internal target-policy collections (for example, the set.discard method of the uncontrolled-execution targets blocklist), remove a denied target from the policy, and then instantiate that otherwise-blocked target, because sibling nodes are processed in insertion order against the same process-global policy. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the permissions of the running application, and the policy mutation persists in process-global state for the lifetime of the Python process. Exploitation requires the application to instantiate attacker-influenced configuration on the legacy path without an execution whitelist; a narrow execution whitelist supplied by trusted Python code is not bypassed by the reported direct mutation path. A fix for the affected Red Hat products is being pursued. Red Hat rates this flaw as Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8); the upstream CVSS v4 score of 8.5 differs due to CVSS version and user-interaction metric differences rather than a different view of the vulnerability.

remediations.details: Avoid passing configuration from untrusted sources to Hydra's instantiate() or to Hydra-controlled Python logging configuration; restrict configuration input to trusted sources. On affected 1.4 development releases, applications can also supply a trusted, narrowly scoped execution whitelist from Python code, and the whitelist itself must not be derived from untrusted configuration. Restart any long-running process that may already have instantiated untrusted configuration, because a policy mutation persists in process-global state for the lifetime of the process. The upstream fix is available in hydra-core 1.3.7 on the stable line and 1.4.0.dev10 on the development line; for the affected Red Hat products, apply product updates containing the fixed version when they become available.

notes.text: A flaw was found in hydra-core. An attacker who supplies or controls a malicious logging configuration can trigger arbitrary code execution by specifying unauthorized Python classes or factory functions. Because Hydra passes logging configuration directly to Python's logging system without enforcing target execution policies, the specified components are invoked with the privileges of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: hydra-core: hydra-core: Arbitrary code execution via unsafe logging configuration
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the hydra-core Python framework, which Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI (RHEL AI) ship as a dependency in their container images. Hydra passes Python logging configuration to logging.config.dictConfig() without applying its target policy to handler class values or to formatter, filter, handler, queue, and listener factories. As a result, an attacker who can supply or control a Hydra logging configuration can select an importable class or factory that is then invoked with the privileges of the running application, resulting in arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that a user or process run the application with an attacker-controlled configuration (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R), and the Red Hat severity of IMPORTANT matches the upstream rating. All affected Red Hat product streams are tracked as delegated affects, and a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams.

notes.text: A flaw was found in hydra-core. The instantiate() mechanism does not properly validate callable targets against its blocklist, allowing execution wrappers and deferred calls to bypass authorization checks. An attacker who convinces an application or user to process untrusted configuration files can exploit this vulnerability to achieve arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: hydra-core: hydra-core: Arbitrary code execution via target blocklist bypass in instantiate()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of Important severity was found in the hydra-core Python configuration framework, which is bundled as a dependency in Red Hat AI Inference Server 3.3 and 3.4 and in Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI 3.4. Hydra's instantiate() mechanism does not properly validate the callable selected by the configuration target field against its blocklist: execution wrappers such as timeit.timeit, executable deserialization through pickle.loads, aliases, callable-returning helpers, generic dispatch, and deferred calls can obscure or defer the effective target and bypass the name-based authorization checks. An attacker who convinces an application or user to process an untrusted Hydra configuration file can use this flaw to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the running application. Red Hat rates this flaw as Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream severity. The affected Red Hat products are tracked with a delegated resolution: the impact has been assessed and a fix is being pursued by the responsible engineering teams.

While it can cause a crash, the impact is limited to availability, and exploitation is unlikely in real-world deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension. This vulnerability involves memory corruption, specifically an out-of-bounds read and a heap buffer overflow, which can be triggered by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. When an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against such a database, an attacker can cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or achieve arbitrary code execution, potentially compromising the system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This flaw in the SQLite FTS5 full-text search extension can lead to arbitrary code execution or denial of service. vulnerabilities.title: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite, specifically within its FTS5 full-text search extension. Attackers can exploit a heap-based buffer overflow by providing a specially crafted database. This crafted database contains malicious metadata that triggers an integer underflow during FTS5 MATCH query processing. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to a crash of the application or allow for arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution and crash via heap-based buffer overflow in FTS5
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension can lead to arbitrary code execution or application crashes due to a heap-based buffer overflow. Exploitation requires an attacker to provide a specially crafted SQLite database, which must then be processed by an application compiled with FTS5 support. While requiring user interaction and local access, the potential for full impact on system resources justifies the Important severity.

cwe.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `tarfile.extractall()` function within Python. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted archive. This archive could bypass security filters by using a hardlink that references a symlink, allowing the symlink to be recreated outside the intended destination directory. This could lead to out-of-destination file reads or writes, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python: cpython: CPython: tarfile extraction filter bypass allows escaping the destination directory
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products that appear in dependency searches under names containing "tarfile" but that are not the CPython standard-library tarfile module are not affected by this flaw. Matches such as the Go packages under github.com/containers/image / go.podman.io/image (.../docker/tarfile and .../docker/internal/tarfile) and the Apache Camel artifacts (camel-tarfile, camel-quarkus-tarfile) are unrelated implementations in other languages and do not include the vulnerable CPython tarfile.extractall() filter logic. The separately packaged PyPI component backports-tarfile is also out of scope for this CVE as assigned: it is not the CPython stdlib module named in the advisory and this CVE tracks the interpreter-provided tarfile shipped in Red Hat python3* packages.

notes.text: A double free issue has been identified in libarchive's RAR5 reader. During parsing of a specially crafted RAR5 archive, the filtered_buf pointer may remain stale after being freed during unpacking state reinitialization. Subsequent processing of another archive entry can trigger a second free of the same memory region, resulting in a double-free condition. Successful exploitation may cause applications using the vulnerable libarchive API to terminate unexpectedly, leading to a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libarchive: Double-Free Vulnerability in RAR5 Decompression Logic via dangling filtered_buf pointer in init_unpack()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Red Hat Product Security has assessed this CVE as 7.5 CVSS with Moderate security Impact. This assessment reflects the library's typical deployment within enterprise software, where libarchive is frequently embedded into automated, network-accessible services that receive and process archives originating from remote sources. In these environments, a specially crafted RAR5 archive may be delivered and processed automatically without requiring direct user interaction, allowing a remote attacker to trigger the vulnerability and cause the affected application or service processing the archive to terminate unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service.

From a standalone library perspective, however, the vulnerable code is only reached when an application opens and processes a crafted RAR5 archive. Evaluating libarchive in isolation, without considering downstream deployment models, the vulnerability more closely aligns with a CVSS score of 5.5-CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H (Moderate), reflecting an Attack Vector of Local (AV:L) and User Interaction Required (UI:R). This is because the crafted archive must first be delivered to and processed by a local application before the vulnerable parsing logic is executed. 

Red Hat's assigned score instead reflects the operational deployment of libarchive in automated, network-facing workloads in downstream environment models rather than the standalone library in isolation.

```

This vulnerability only affects libarchive releases that include support for the RAR5 archive format. RAR5 support was first introduced upstream in libarchive 3.4.0 (https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/wiki/ReleaseNotes#libarchive-340). Earlier libarchive releases do not contain the vulnerable RAR5 parsing code and are therefore not affected.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, and 8 ship Libarchive versions prior to v3.4.0 that do not include RAR5 support and are therefore not affected.

```

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A denial-of-service and resource exhaustion vulnerability exists within the `GDBus` component of GLib. The `gdbusauth` authentication mechanism fails to enforce proper length limitations on data lines read from a client. An unauthenticated local or remote attacker can exploit this lack of input validation by sending excessively long streams of data, causing the application to consume massive amounts of system memory and CPU, potentially leading to a crash or system hang.

notes.text: GDBusServer: glib2: GDBusServer pre-authentication DoS via unbounded SASL line buffering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `GDBus` component of GLib. A local or remote unauthenticated attacker could send an engineered stream of data without line length limitations during the authentication process (`gdbusauth`), leading to excessive memory allocation and CPU consumption. This resource exhaustion can result in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition, causing applications or services dependent on GLib to become unstable or crash.

notes.text: A flaw was found in xdgmime. A heap-based buffer overflow can be triggered in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in the xdgmimemagic.c file on little-endian systems when an attacker-controlled MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) is parsed by an application performing MIME type detection (e.g., via g_content_type_guess()). When performing byte-swap, incorrect pointer arithmetic on the write side causes an out-of-bounds write of 2 bytes, resulting in an application crash or memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: xdgmime: heap-based buffer overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in xdgmimemagic.c
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker must convince a user to install a malicious MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) and process it with an application performing MIME type detection, limiting its exposure. Also, only little-endian systems are vulnerable. Due to these reasons, this issue has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in urllib3, an HTTP client library for Python. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause excessive resource consumption, such as high CPU usage and massive memory allocation, on the client side. This occurs when urllib3 attempts to decompress an entire HTTP response, even if only a partial read was requested, or when draining the connection after a partial decompression. This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Vim, a widely used command-line text editor. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system. By opening a specially crafted Python file and then triggering the omni-completion feature, the attacker can cause Vim to run malicious code from a sibling Python package. This could lead to a complete compromise of the user's system.

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in Vim that allows a local attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution. The flaw occurs when a user opens a specially crafted Python file and invokes omni-completion, leading to the execution of malicious code from a co-located Python package. This risk is present in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other products where Vim is deployed with Python omni-completion enabled, potentially compromising the editing user's system.

remediations.details: Users can mitigate this vulnerability by disabling Python omni-completion in Vim if it is not essential for their workflow. This prevents the execution of untrusted Python code when opening hostile files. To disable this feature, ensure that the `omnifunc` option in your Vim configuration (e.g., `~/.vimrc`) is not set to `pythoncomplete#Complete` or `python3complete#Complete`. Alternatively, users should avoid invoking omni-completion (`Ctrl-X Ctrl-O`) on Python files from untrusted sources. Disabling Python omni-completion may affect Python development functionality within Vim.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `acl` package, specifically within its `libacl` pathname-based functions. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by using a symbolic link to replace a pathname component. This could allow the attacker to redirect access control list (ACL) read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, leading to unauthorized manipulation of ACLs and ultimately local privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a local attacker who controls any component of a pathname processed by a privileged process using libacl can redirect ACL operations to arbitrary files. Exploitation requires local access with the ability to create symlinks in a directory that a privileged program later processes with acl_get_file() or acl_set_file(). In default RHEL and OpenShift CoreOS configurations, standard file permission settings limit where unprivileged users can create symlinks, reducing the practical attack surface. Programs that operate on user-supplied paths with elevated privileges are most at risk.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module. This vulnerability, categorized as an Observable Timing Discrepancy (CWE-208), allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords. By repeatedly attempting authentication and measuring response-timing differences during plaintext password comparison, an attacker can deduce the password. This flaw is exploitable when the `pam_userdb` module is configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default setting.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing discrepancy in pam_userdb module
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords through a timing discrepancy. This vulnerability requires the `pam_userdb` module to be explicitly configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default or recommended configuration in Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments. The impact is limited by the need for repeated authentication attempts and specific, non-default module configurations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. An off-by-one error can occur in the gvs_tuple_is_normal function in the glib/gvariant-serialiser.c file when doing an alignment padding check because the bounds check uses > instead of >=, causing an out-of-bounds read of only 1 byte. This issue can cause a minor information disclosure of 1 byte and a denial of service when the out-of-bounds read crosses a page boundary.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: buffer over-read in glib/gvariant-serialiser.c via gvs_tuple_is_normal()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications calling the `g_variant_is_normal_form()`, `g_variant_get_normal_form()` or `g_variant_byteswap()` functions that process untrusted GVariant data received from D-Bus, network or file are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause an out-of-bounds read of only 1 byte, leading to an information disclosure of only 1 byte and a denial of service when the out-of-bounds read crosses a page boundary. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. An out-of-bounds read of only 2 bytes can occur in the g_date_time_get_ymd function in the glib/gdatetime.c file when an invalid GDateTime object produced by the g_date_time_add_full function is processed. This flaw can corrupt the date output and potentially cause logic errors that may lead to a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: out-of-bounds read in glib/gdatetime.c:g_date_time_get_ymd via invalid GDateTime
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications that allow a user to submit a date to `g_date_time_add_full()` and later call any getter functions, such as `g_date_time_get_month()` or `g_date_time_get_year()`, with the returned GDateTime object are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause an out-of-bounds read of only 2 bytes, leading to a denial of service due to logic errors that a corrupted date can trigger. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. A buffer over-read can occur in the g_regex_replace function when used with the `G_REGEX_RAW` compile flag and case-change replacement escapes because the string_append function processes matched substrings using UTF-8 functions that assume valid UTF-8 input, even when the string is treated as raw bytes. This vulnerability can cause a minor information disclosure of 1-5 bytes and a denial of service when the buffer over-read crosses a page boundary.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: buffer over-read in g_regex_replace() via glib/gregex.c:string_append() and g_utf8_next_char()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications that use g_regex_replace() or g_regex_replace_eval() with the G_REGEX_RAW compile flag and allow user-controlled replacement strings containing case-change escapes (\u, \l, \U, \L) are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause a buffer over-read of 1-5 bytes, leading to a minor information disclosure and a denial of service when the buffer over-read crosses a page boundary. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. The D-Bus client-side implementation of the DBUS_COOKIE_SHA1 SASL authentication mechanism does not validate the cookie_context parameter received from the server. A malicious D-Bus server can supply a cookie_context containing path traversal sequences, causing the client to read an arbitrary file and exfiltrate sensitive data by verifying guessed file contents against a generated hash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: path traversal in glib/gio/gdbusauthmechanismsha1.c via keyring_lookup_entry and mechanism_client_data_receive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be in a position to perform a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack on the connection or operate a malicious server that the client connects to. Furthermore, extracting data requires an oracle attack (guessing and hashing), increasing the complexity of exploitation. However, if successful, this issue allows the exfiltration of sensitive secrets, such as SSH keys or API tokens, from the filesystem. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Vim, an open-source command-line text editor. The PHP omni-completion script improperly handles specially crafted input. When a victim opens a malicious PHP file and invokes omni-completion, an unescaped class or trait name can be interpreted as Ex commands. This allows a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary operating-system command execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via crafted PHP file in omni-completion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has rated this vulnerability as having a Moderate impact. While successful exploitation allows for arbitrary operating-system command execution when a user opens a crafted PHP file and triggers omni-completion, this feature is disabled by default in Red Hat products. The requirement for a non-default configuration, combined with mandatory user interaction, significantly reduces the real-world risk."

This could allow an attacker to take control of the affected system.

cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

notes.text: A flaw was found in FFmpeg. A remote attacker can exploit an infinite loop vulnerability in the RTP/ASF demuxer by sending a specially crafted stream. This vulnerability occurs because the rtp_asf_fix_header function does not properly validate the size of data chunks, preventing the processing loop from advancing. Successful exploitation leads to CPU exhaustion, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: FFmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted RTP/ASF stream
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The impact rating reflects that this issue strictly impacts Availability (A:H) with low/no effect on Confidentiality or Integrity. Exploitation requires an active application to ingest and demux a maliciously crafted RTP/ASF media stream; passive files at rest pose no risk. 

Successful exploitation results in high CPU consumption that stalls the stream-processing thread or container worker, but it does not cause memory corruption or allow arbitrary code execution. Systems that do not dynamically ingest untrusted, real-time RTP/ASF network streams are effectively out of scope for operational disruption.

By providing specially crafted file names in the metadata, an attacker can trick the system into including sensitive local files when datasets are saved or published, leading to information disclosure.

notes.text: datasets: Datasets: Information disclosure via path traversal vulnerability
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This path traversal vulnerability in the `datasets` library allows for information disclosure. An attacker could exploit this by providing specially crafted `file_name` metadata to a folder-based dataset builder, which, upon user interaction with `save_to_disk` or `push_to_hub` operations, could embed arbitrary local files into the output. The requirement for user interaction reduces the overall risk.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FFmpeg. A remote attacker can exploit a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability within the `vf_hqdn3d` filter by providing a specially crafted video file. When filtergraph reinitialization is disabled, the filter allocates undersized memory buffers for video frames. Subsequent larger frames can cause the application to write beyond these allocated boundaries, leading to heap memory corruption. This can result in arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Hugging Face Accelerate. This path traversal vulnerability exists in the `load_checkpoint_in_model` and `load_checkpoint_and_dispatch` functions due to a failure to sanitize `weight_map` entries from sharded checkpoint indexes. An attacker can exploit this by supplying relative paths with `../` sequences or absolute paths, leading to the ability to read arbitrary files or cause a denial of service by pointing shard entries at named pipes.

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in Hugging Face Accelerate that could lead to arbitrary file disclosure and denial of service. While requiring user interaction, an attacker could craft malicious `weight_map` entries in sharded checkpoint indexes to exploit path traversal, impacting the confidentiality and availability of systems utilizing affected Red Hat AI/ML products.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. An attacker can exploit this by submitting specially crafted video requests that force the use of the PyNvVideoCodec GPU decoder. This bypasses the engine's static GPU memory reservation, allowing the attacker to exhaust shared GPU memory. The consequence is a denial of service (DoS), leading to request failures or worker crashes.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: GPU memory exhaustion via PyNvVideoCodec decode bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity denial-of-service flaw was found in vLLM, the inference and serving engine shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) vLLM-based components. A remote attacker with privileges to submit requests to a video-capable GPU deployment where the PyNvVideoCodec GPU decoder is installed can send specially crafted video requests that set media_io_kwargs.video.video_backend to pynvvideocodec, forcing use of the PyNvVideoCodec decoder even when the startup configuration selected a software decoder. Because the engine reserves decoder memory only according to its static configuration, the request-selected decoder's CUDA context, decoder surfaces, and decoded-frame allocations are not removed from the KV-cache budget, allowing the attacker to exhaust shared GPU memory and cause request failures, worker crashes, or denial of service. Red Hat rated this flaw MODERATE with CVSS 3.1 score 6.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), consistent with the upstream rating; the impact is limited to availability, with no confidentiality or integrity impact. Affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and OpenShift AI components are marked DEFER because Red Hat does not file trackers for MODERATE severity flaws with a CVSS score below 7.0; the fix is deferred to a future product update, and the residual risk is denial of service on deployments that accept video requests on GPU hardware with PyNvVideoCodec installed. Deployments that do not process video requests or do not have the PyNvVideoCodec decoder installed are not exposed to this attack path.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM. An authenticated API client can exploit derender endpoints by providing oversized GenerateResponse objects. These endpoints process the objects without enforcing output bounds or response-size limits. This can lead to excessive consumption of CPU and memory resources, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Denial of Service via unbounded token ID decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity denial of service flaw was found in vLLM, the LLM inference and serving engine shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI. The /v1/completions/derender and /v1/chat/completions/derender API endpoints accept caller-supplied GenerateResponse objects and process their generate_responses, choices, token_ids, prompt_logprobs, logprobs.content, top_logprobs, and routed_experts structures through OnlineDerenderer and tokenizer.decode before limits such as max_model_len, max_tokens, max_num_seqs, or response-size restrictions are enforced. As a result, an authenticated API client can submit oversized GenerateResponse objects and cause excessive CPU and memory consumption, potentially producing oversized responses and degrading or denying service for other users of the vLLM instance. The affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI streams are currently marked for a deferred fix; until a remediated update is delivered, deployments that expose the vLLM API to lower-trust authenticated clients retain residual risk of resource-exhaustion attacks. Red Hat and upstream both rate this issue Moderate (CVSS 4.3, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L), reflecting the availability-only impact and the credentials required to exploit it.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tesseract, an open-source Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engine. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted .traineddata LSTM model component. When Tesseract's deserializer processes this component during OCR recognition, an unchecked integer multiplication can occur, leading to an undersized buffer and a heap out-of-bounds write. This vulnerability could result in a denial of service or potentially arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A vulnerability in Vim allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands by crafting a malicious .VimballRecord file that injects OS commands executed when processed by the vimball#RmVimball() function.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vim: Vim: Arbitrary command execution via crafted vimball
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in Vim where a crafted vimball can lead to arbitrary command execution. The flaw allows an attacker to embed malicious commands within a `.VimballRecord` file, which are then executed with user privileges during a later, unrelated vimball installation or removal. This extends the impact of processing untrusted vimball files beyond the initial installation.

remediations.details:
To mitigate this vulnerability, users can disable the `keywordprg` option for shell script filetypes. This prevents Vim from executing external commands via the `K` command with potentially untrusted input. Create or edit the following files in your Vim configuration directory:

- `~/.vim/after/ftplugin/sh.vim`: `setlocal keywordprg=`
- `~/.vim/after/ftplugin/zsh.vim`: `setlocal keywordprg=`
- `~/.vim/after/ftplugin/ps1.vim`: `setlocal keywordprg=`

This change takes effect the next time a shell script is opened in Vim.

cwe.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. Unauthenticated attackers can send malformed JSON requests to various API endpoints, triggering validation errors. The system's error handling mechanism converts these validation errors into strings without properly sanitizing traceback-style file paths. This vulnerability allows for the disclosure of sensitive internal system information, including the operating system username, home and virtual environment paths, Python version, internal package structure, and handler function names.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Information Disclosure via Validation Error Messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate: vLLM, as deployed in Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat OpenShift AI, is susceptible to information disclosure. Unauthenticated, malformed JSON requests to its API endpoints can expose sensitive system details, including OS usernames, file paths, Python version, and internal package structure, due to insufficient sanitization of validation error messages.

vulnerabilities.title: vllm: vLLM: Information Disclosure via Validation Error Messages

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the lm-format-enforcer backend. By submitting a specially crafted regular expression through the structured_outputs.regex parameter, the attacker can cause the system to consume excessive CPU resources. This leads to a denial of service, stalling the structured-output engine and preventing legitimate requests from being processed.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Denial of Service via Regular Expression processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw in vLLM is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS). By sending a specially crafted regular expression to the `/v1/completions` endpoint, the attacker can cause the vLLM service to consume excessive CPU resources, leading to a complete stall of the structured-output engine and preventing legitimate requests.
notes.title: Statement

This is particularly relevant in multi-tenant environments where vLLM processes requests concurrently from different users.

vulnerabilities.title: vllm: vLLM: Denial of Service via unbounded completion prompt lists

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models. The MiMoV2OmniMultiModalProcessor component improperly handles attacker-controlled image and audio strings, bypassing security protections. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and read arbitrary local files accessible to the vLLM process. Successful exploitation could lead to unauthorized access to internal network resources, cloud metadata, and sensitive local system files.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: vLLM: Server-Side Request Forgery and arbitrary file read via improper media processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity flaw was found in the vLLM inference and serving engine as shipped in Red Hat AI Inference Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI. The MiMoV2OmniMultiModalProcessor in vllm/transformers_utils/processors/mimo_v2_omni.py passes attacker-controlled image and audio strings through _fetch_image, requests.get, and Image.open instead of the MediaConnector, bypassing the allowed_media_domains and allowed_local_media_path protections. A remote attacker able to submit multimodal requests to a vLLM server can use crafted image or audio strings to make the server issue requests to attacker-chosen URLs (server-side request forgery) and read arbitrary local files accessible to the vLLM process, potentially exposing internal network resources, cloud metadata services, and sensitive local system files. The Red Hat severity of Moderate (CVSS 6.5) is consistent with the upstream assessment. All currently affected Red Hat product streams ship vLLM versions that contain this flaw, and the fix is deferred: the upstream fix has not yet been incorporated into the affected Red Hat AI Inference Server and RHEL AI streams, leaving deployments that accept untrusted multimodal input at residual risk of information disclosure through server-side requests and local file reads.

notes.text: A flaw was found in httpx2, a Python HTTP client. The Server-Sent Events (SSE) parser in httpx2 can be exploited by a remote attacker. By sending a specially crafted stream where an unterminated line is split across many response chunks, the parser repeatedly copies and rescans buffered text. This quadratic processing work consumes excessive CPU resources, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by blocking synchronous workers or asynchronous event loops.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate: A denial of service vulnerability exists in the HTTPX2 Python client library, affecting Red Hat products such as Lightspeed Core and Red Hat OpenShift AI. This flaw allows a remote attacker to consume excessive CPU resources by sending a specially crafted Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream, leading to resource exhaustion. The impact is limited to availability and requires interaction with a malicious or compromised SSE endpoint.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

notes.text: A flaw was found in HTTPX2, a Python HTTP client. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted multipart/form-data requests. The `FileField.render_headers()` function fails to validate `Content-Type` values and custom headers, allowing the injection of Carriage Return (CR) or Line Feed (LF) characters. This could lead to the injection of arbitrary part headers, potentially altering the interpretation of multipart data or bypassing security checks by a downstream parser.

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

notes.text: A flaw was found in HTTPX2, a Python HTTP client. The `Request._prepare()` function can incorrectly add a `Content-Length` header to a request that already includes a `Transfer-Encoding` header. notes.text: A flaw was found in httpcore2, a component used by HTTPX2. When a remote origin uses WebSocket Secure (wss) through a SOCKS5 proxy, httpcore2 fails to initiate Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption because its upgrade condition only recognizes HTTPS. This vulnerability allows an attacker controlling or observing the proxy path to intercept and read sensitive WebSocket traffic, including authentication details and data frames, as it is transmitted in plaintext. The attacker could also modify the traffic or impersonate the WebSocket server, leading to information disclosure and potential compromise of communication integrity.

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

notes.text: A flaw was found in httpx2, a Python HTTP client. The content decoders in httpx2 fully inflate compressed network chunks (such as gzip, deflate, br, or zstd) before yielding bounded pieces to the application. This can lead to a small compressed chunk expanding significantly in memory, for example, a 64 KiB chunk expanding to approximately 64 MiB. A remote attacker, by controlling or compromising a server, could exploit this vulnerability to cause severe memory pressure or out-of-memory process termination, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) for applications using httpx2.

Standard token validation workflows that enforce signature verification prior to payload parsing remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: pyjwt: Denial of Service via deeply nested token headers

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. A remote attacker can forge authentication tokens and bypass security controls by signing tokens with an empty key. When verifying tokens against a JSON Web Key (JWK) set that contains an empty Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) key, the library fails to enforce key-length validation. This allows an attacker to generate valid tokens carrying arbitrary claims to gain unauthorized access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Authentication bypass via empty HMAC key acceptance
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact for Red Hat products because successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to generate forged tokens with arbitrary administrative claims, completely bypassing authentication controls. The flaw is not classified as Critical because exploitation requires a specific misconfiguration prerequisite—the target environment must actively load a symmetric key set containing a blank key entry. Typical deployments running standard authentication configurations are not exposed unless an empty HMAC key definition is explicitly ingested by the application.

vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: pyjwt: Authentication bypass via empty HMAC key acceptance

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When retrieving cryptographic keys from a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint, PyJWKClient fails to validate HTTP redirect destinations against trusted domain boundaries. A remote attacker who can influence the response of a trusted endpoint can redirect key requests to an untrusted server, allowing the client to accept forged verification keys or potentially exposing sensitive credentials.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because improper handling of HTTP redirects during dynamic key retrieval can allow an adversary to supply forged cryptographic keys or intercept sensitive request headers. In Red Hat environments where services utilize PyJWKClient to fetch JSON Web Key Sets over the network, accepting untrusted key material may compromise token validation and authentication boundaries. Exploitation requires the target service to dynamically resolve keys via HTTP and relies on an attacker's ability to manipulate responses returned by the configured key server.

vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: pyjwt: Verification key substitution via unvalidated JWKS redirects

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When an application allows both symmetric and asymmetric signing algorithms, minor formatting variations in a public key can prevent the library from properly identifying it as an asymmetric key. Consequently, the library improperly treats the public key as a shared secret key, allowing a remote attacker to forge valid authentication tokens and bypass security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: PyJWT: Authentication bypass via improper public key validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker could forge valid cryptographic tokens and bypass authentication checks without knowing the private signing key. Exploitation occurs when consuming applications configure token verification to accept both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms simultaneously, allowing an asymmetric public key to be mishandled as a symmetric secret. Deployments that strictly enforce a single algorithm type or validate tokens using JSON Web Key sets do not permit this algorithm confusion and remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. When decoding JSON Web Token (JWT) signature segments, the library accepts characters outside the standard Base64URL encoding format. A remote attacker can exploit this issue by appending extra characters to a valid token signature, creating an alternate token representation that decodes to the identical signature. Consequently, this can allow an attacker to bypass raw-token revocation checks or blocklists that rely on exact string matching.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing crafted certificate-like input containing repeated start markers without matching end markers. This malformed input triggers excessive regular expression backtracking during validation in the is_pem_format function, consuming high central processing unit (CPU) resources and potentially making the application unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Denial of Service via regular expression backtracking in is_pem_format
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate because although an attacker can trigger CPU exhaustion leading to denial of service, successful exploitation requires an application to accept and parse untrusted, attacker-supplied key or certificate input. In standard Red Hat product configurations, cryptographic verification keys are sourced from trusted local files or managed credential stores rather than arbitrary external inputs. As a result, typical deployments are not directly exposed unless an application explicitly ingests unvalidated key material.

vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: pyjwt: Denial of Service via regular expression backtracking in is_pem_format

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. The library fails to identify asymmetric public keys supplied in Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) format, inadvertently treating the public data as a shared secret in Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) operations. If an application supports both asymmetric and symmetric signing algorithms, a remote attacker knowing the public key can exploit this flaw to forge valid authentication tokens and bypass access controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: PyJWT: Authentication bypass via acceptance of DER public keys as HMAC secrets
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an attacker can forge valid JSON Web Tokens and bypass authentication mechanisms if public cryptographic keys are mistakenly treated as shared secrets. Exploitation requires a specific application scenario where both asymmetric and HMAC algorithms are concurrently permitted during signature verification and public keys are provided in raw DER binary format. Typical Red Hat product integrations do not employ this vulnerable algorithm combination or key encoding by default, which restricts the overall attack surface in standard production environments.

vulnerabilities.title: pyjwt: PyJWT: Authentication bypass via acceptance of DER public keys as HMAC secrets

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. When verifying cryptographic keys, the raw JSON Web Key (JWK) parser fails to normalize Unicode byte-order marks (BOM). In mixed-algorithm verification environments, an attacker who knows the public key can supply a key prefixed with a byte-order mark, causing the system to misidentify the public key as a shared symmetric secret. This flaw allows an attacker to forge authenticated JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and bypass authentication controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Token forgery via improper Unicode byte-order mark handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because successful exploitation permits an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and forge valid tokens, though exploitation requires specific mixed-algorithm verification settings. In Red Hat environments, exposure is restricted to services that simultaneously allow both symmetric HMAC and asymmetric signature algorithms while parsing public keys that contain byte order marks. Workloads and services that enforce single-algorithm verification policies or utilize standard asymmetric key validation routines are not susceptible to this attack.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication by forging arbitrary JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). Exploitation is limited to environments where applications concurrently permit symmetric HMAC and asymmetric algorithms while passing public key containers into validation routines.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. The library fails to properly handle errors when parsing a JSON Web Key (JWK) set that contains a malformed RSA key alongside valid keys. A remote attacker can supply or inject a malformed key to abort the processing of the entire key set, resulting in authentication failures and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pyjwt: pyjwt: Denial of Service via malformed RSA key in JWK set
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity for Red Hat products because an attacker can only cause service disruptions without compromising cryptographic keys or bypassing signature validation. The issue is triggered when an application ingests an untrusted key bundle containing an invalid RSA entry, causing key set processing to terminate prematurely due to an unhandled exception. Because exploitation requires consuming malformed key sets from identity providers and only affects availability rather than enabling unauthorized access, the blast radius is contained.

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyjwt. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass token validation checks when an application reuses an options configuration across multiple token decoding requests. Because the library unintentionally modifies the caller's shared configuration dictionary when signature verification is disabled, subsequent token verifications may retain disabled claim checks. As a result, an attacker could supply an expired or otherwise invalid JSON Web Token (JWT) that the application accepts as valid.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fsspec. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by tricking an application into loading a maliciously crafted reference document, such as a Kerchunk metadata file. When the reference filesystem is opened, unrestricted template evaluation executes embedded expressions in the context of the running process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fsspec: fsspec: Arbitrary code execution via crafted reference documents
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the fsspec Python package, which is bundled as a dependency in multiple Red Hat products, including Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat AI Inference Server, and Ansible Automation Platform. The ReferenceFileSystem implementation in fsspec renders fields from Kerchunk reference JSON documents using unrestricted Jinja2 template evaluation (jinja2.Template(...).render(...)). A remote attacker who tricks a user or application into loading a maliciously crafted reference document, supplied inline or fetched from an attacker-controlled URL, for example through consumers such as xarray, can execute arbitrary Python code in the context of the running process when the reference filesystem is opened, before any referenced data is read. This can fully compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected process. Red Hat rates this issue as IMPORTANT (CVSS 8.8: AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), which matches the upstream severity assessment. The affected Red Hat products are marked affected with resolution delegated to the responsible product teams, and a fix is being pursued.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in multidict. The multidict C extension fails to release object references during certain items-view union and subtraction operations. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted input sequences to applications performing these operations, triggering uncollectable memory leaks. This issue can cause unbounded process memory growth, ultimately leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: multidict: multidict: Denial of Service via memory leak in items-view operations
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact for Red Hat products because triggering the memory leak requires an application to evaluate specific items-view set operations against untrusted user input, which is uncommon across standard deployments. While multiple Red Hat services bundle multidict, exploitation is limited to gradual memory exhaustion and denial of service, with no possibility of remote code execution or data disclosure. Furthermore, standard dictionary access patterns, forward unions, and intersections are not susceptible to this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the interactive shell of the xmllint command-line tool, used for parsing XML files. When a user inputs an overly long command, the program does not check the input size properly, which can cause it to crash. This issue might allow attackers to run harmful code in rare configurations without modern protections.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libxml2: Stack Buffer Overflow in xmllint Interactive Shell Command Handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The Red Hat Product Security team has rated the severity of this vulnerability as Low, since it affects only the interactive shell mode of the xmllint tool and requires a user to manually run the tool and enter or receive specially crafted input. The exploitation requires local access and a highly specific usage scenario that is uncommon in typical environments. While it can cause a crash, the impact is limited to availability, and exploitation is unlikely in real-world deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension. This vulnerability involves memory corruption, specifically an out-of-bounds read and a heap buffer overflow, which can be triggered by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. When an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against such a database, an attacker can cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or achieve arbitrary code execution, potentially compromising the system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This flaw in the SQLite FTS5 full-text search extension can lead to arbitrary code execution or denial of service. Exploitation requires an application to process a specially crafted SQLite database containing malformed FTS5 page data, which could occur if an attacker provides a malicious database to a vulnerable application. This risk is elevated in scenarios where applications handle untrusted SQLite database files.

vulnerabilities.title: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FTS5 full-text search data

notes.text: A flaw was found in SQLite, specifically within its FTS5 full-text search extension. Attackers can exploit a heap-based buffer overflow by providing a specially crafted database. This crafted database contains malicious metadata that triggers an integer underflow during FTS5 MATCH query processing. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to a crash of the application or allow for arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: sqlite: SQLite: Arbitrary code execution and crash via heap-based buffer overflow in FTS5
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in SQLite's FTS5 full-text search extension can lead to arbitrary code execution or application crashes due to a heap-based buffer overflow. Exploitation requires an attacker to provide a specially crafted SQLite database, which must then be processed by an application compiled with FTS5 support. While requiring user interaction and local access, the potential for full impact on system resources justifies the Important severity.

cwe.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `tarfile.extractall()` function within Python. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted archive. This archive could bypass security filters by using a hardlink that references a symlink, allowing the symlink to be recreated outside the intended destination directory. This could lead to out-of-destination file reads or writes, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary file modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python: cpython: CPython: tarfile extraction filter bypass allows escaping the destination directory
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products that appear in dependency searches under names containing "tarfile" but that are not the CPython standard-library tarfile module are not affected by this flaw. Matches such as the Go packages under github.com/containers/image / go.podman.io/image (.../docker/tarfile and .../docker/internal/tarfile) and the Apache Camel artifacts (camel-tarfile, camel-quarkus-tarfile) are unrelated implementations in other languages and do not include the vulnerable CPython tarfile.extractall() filter logic. The separately packaged PyPI component backports-tarfile is also out of scope for this CVE as assigned: it is not the CPython stdlib module named in the advisory and this CVE tracks the interpreter-provided tarfile shipped in Red Hat python3* packages.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in pip. When processing doubly-encoded package URLs from malicious package indexes, pip incorrectly handles the file paths. A remote attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to download or install a package from such an index. This could allow for files to be installed to arbitrary locations on the system, potentially leading to system compromise. notes.text: A flaw was found in xdgmime. A heap-based buffer overflow can be triggered in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in the xdgmimemagic.c file on little-endian systems when an attacker-controlled MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) is parsed by an application performing MIME type detection (e.g., via g_content_type_guess()). When performing byte-swap, incorrect pointer arithmetic on the write side causes an out-of-bounds write of 2 bytes, resulting in an application crash or memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: xdgmime: heap-based buffer overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in xdgmimemagic.c
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker must convince a user to install a malicious MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) and process it with an application performing MIME type detection, limiting its exposure. Also, only little-endian systems are vulnerable. Due to these reasons, this issue has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in oauthlib. When JSON with Padding (JSONP) support is enabled on the token revocation endpoint, the application fails to validate user-supplied callback parameters before reflecting them into the response. A remote attacker could exploit this flaw by submitting a crafted callback value, allowing the execution of arbitrary JavaScript code within the security context of client applications consuming the response.

notes.text: oauthlib: oauthlib: Unsafe JSONP callback injection in RevocationEndpoint allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because successful exploitation requires a non-default configuration alongside user interaction to execute injected script within the client application's origin. In typical deployments, JSONP processing is disabled by default within oauthlib, leaving standard configurations unaffected. Exposure is limited to custom services that explicitly activate JSONP handling on the token revocation endpoint and process untrusted callback inputs.

remediations.details: JSONP support on oauthlib's token revocation endpoint is opt-in and disabled by default. Deployments can mitigate this issue by not enabling it: ensure enable_jsonp=True is not passed when constructing oauthlib's RevocationEndpoint, so that user-supplied callback parameters are never reflected into JavaScript response bodies. notes.text: A flaw was found in oauthlib. A timing side-channel vulnerability in the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) validation process allows a remote attacker to recover secret verification codes. Because comparison operations do not execute in constant time, an attacker who has intercepted an authorization code can measure response latency differences across repeated requests to infer the expected verification code character-by-character. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to exchange the authorization code for an access token and impersonate the victim user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: oauthlib: oauthlib: Timing attack vulnerability in PKCE code_verifier/code_challenge comparison allows authorization code recovery
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because successful exploitation requires multiple stringent prerequisites, including intercepting a valid authorization code, measuring high-resolution network response times, and an OAuth server implementation that permits repeated verification attempts without revoking the code. While oauthlib facilitates PKCE validation in OAuth 2.0 deployments across Red Hat environments, the timing discrepancies are minor and highly susceptible to network noise in real-world scenarios. Consequently, extracting secret verifiers remotely presents significant practical hurdles.
notes.title: Statement

remediations.details: Users can mitigate this vulnerability by disabling Python omni-completion in Vim if it is not essential for their workflow. This prevents the execution of untrusted Python code when opening hostile files. To disable this feature, ensure that the `omnifunc` option in your Vim configuration (e.g., `~/.vimrc`) is not set to `pythoncomplete#Complete` or `python3complete#Complete`. Alternatively, users should avoid invoking omni-completion (`Ctrl-X Ctrl-O`) on Python files from untrusted sources. Disabling Python omni-completion may affect Python development functionality within Vim.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `acl` package, specifically within its `libacl` pathname-based functions. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by using a symbolic link to replace a pathname component. This could allow the attacker to redirect access control list (ACL) read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, leading to unauthorized manipulation of ACLs and ultimately local privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a local attacker who controls any component of a pathname processed by a privileged process using libacl can redirect ACL operations to arbitrary files. Exploitation requires local access with the ability to create symlinks in a directory that a privileged program later processes with acl_get_file() or acl_set_file(). In default RHEL and OpenShift CoreOS configurations, standard file permission settings limit where unprivileged users can create symlinks, reducing the practical attack surface. Programs that operate on user-supplied paths with elevated privileges are most at risk.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module. This vulnerability, categorized as an Observable Timing Discrepancy (CWE-208), allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords. By repeatedly attempting authentication and measuring response-timing differences during plaintext password comparison, an attacker can deduce the password. This flaw is exploitable when the `pam_userdb` module is configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default setting.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing discrepancy in pam_userdb module
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in Linux-PAM's `pam_userdb` module allows a local or network-adjacent attacker to recover plaintext passwords through a timing discrepancy. This vulnerability requires the `pam_userdb` module to be explicitly configured to store and compare credentials in plaintext, which is not a default or recommended configuration in Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments. The impact is limited by the need for repeated authentication attempts and specific, non-default module configurations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. An off-by-one error can occur in the gvs_tuple_is_normal function in the glib/gvariant-serialiser.c file when doing an alignment padding check because the bounds check uses > instead of >=, causing an out-of-bounds read of only 1 byte. This issue can cause a minor information disclosure of 1 byte and a denial of service when the out-of-bounds read crosses a page boundary.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: buffer over-read in glib/gvariant-serialiser.c via gvs_tuple_is_normal()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications calling the `g_variant_is_normal_form()`, `g_variant_get_normal_form()` or `g_variant_byteswap()` functions that process untrusted GVariant data received from D-Bus, network or file are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause an out-of-bounds read of only 1 byte, leading to an information disclosure of only 1 byte and a denial of service when the out-of-bounds read crosses a page boundary. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. An out-of-bounds read of only 2 bytes can occur in the g_date_time_get_ymd function in the glib/gdatetime.c file when an invalid GDateTime object produced by the g_date_time_add_full function is processed. This flaw can corrupt the date output and potentially cause logic errors that may lead to a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: out-of-bounds read in glib/gdatetime.c:g_date_time_get_ymd via invalid GDateTime
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications that allow a user to submit a date to `g_date_time_add_full()` and later call any getter functions, such as `g_date_time_get_month()` or `g_date_time_get_year()`, with the returned GDateTime object are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause an out-of-bounds read of only 2 bytes, leading to a denial of service due to logic errors that a corrupted date can trigger. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. A buffer over-read can occur in the g_regex_replace function when used with the `G_REGEX_RAW` compile flag and case-change replacement escapes because the string_append function processes matched substrings using UTF-8 functions that assume valid UTF-8 input, even when the string is treated as raw bytes. This vulnerability can cause a minor information disclosure of 1-5 bytes and a denial of service when the buffer over-read crosses a page boundary.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: buffer over-read in g_regex_replace() via glib/gregex.c:string_append() and g_utf8_next_char()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Any applications that use g_regex_replace() or g_regex_replace_eval() with the G_REGEX_RAW compile flag and allow user-controlled replacement strings containing case-change escapes (\u, \l, \U, \L) are vulnerable to this issue. This flaw can cause a buffer over-read of 1-5 bytes, leading to a minor information disclosure and a denial of service when the buffer over-read crosses a page boundary. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in GLib. The D-Bus client-side implementation of the DBUS_COOKIE_SHA1 SASL authentication mechanism does not validate the cookie_context parameter received from the server. A malicious D-Bus server can supply a cookie_context containing path traversal sequences, causing the client to read an arbitrary file and exfiltrate sensitive data by verifying guessed file contents against a generated hash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: glib: path traversal in glib/gio/gdbusauthmechanismsha1.c via keyring_lookup_entry and mechanism_client_data_receive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be in a position to perform a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack on the connection or operate a malicious server that the client connects to. Furthermore, extracting data requires an oracle attack (guessing and hashing), increasing the complexity of exploitation. However, if successful, this issue allows the exfiltration of sensitive secrets, such as SSH keys or API tokens, from the filesystem. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyTorch Lightning. This vulnerability allows attackers to achieve remote code execution by crafting malicious checkpoint files. These files exploit a weakness in the _load_state function, which imports and executes attacker-controlled module names from checkpoint instantiator hyperparameters, bypassing existing security protections.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pytorch-lightning: PyTorch Lightning: Remote code execution via malicious checkpoint files
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important severity flaw in PyTorch Lightning that could lead to remote code execution. The vulnerability arises from the _load_state function's ability to import and execute attacker-controlled module names from maliciously crafted checkpoint files, even when weights_only=True is enabled. Exploitation requires a local attacker to trick a user into loading a specially crafted checkpoint file.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Vim, an open-source command-line text editor. The PHP omni-completion script improperly handles specially crafted input. When a victim opens a malicious PHP file and invokes omni-completion, an unescaped class or trait name can be interpreted as Ex commands. This allows a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary operating-system command execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via crafted PHP file in omni-completion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has rated this vulnerability as having a Moderate impact. While successful exploitation allows for arbitrary operating-system command execution when a user opens a crafted PHP file and triggers omni-completion, this feature is disabled by default in Red Hat products. The requirement for a non-default configuration, combined with mandatory user interaction, significantly reduces the real-world risk."

To prevent exploitation, the PHP omni-completion script can be disabled by moving or renaming `phpcomplete.vim`. notes.text: A command injection vulnerability in Vim's C omni-completion script allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands if a user is tricked into opening a maliciously crafted tags file and manually invoking the autocomplete feature.

notes.text: This Moderate flaw in Vim's C omni-completion script allows for arbitrary command execution. Exploitation requires a user to open a specially crafted C source file along with a malicious project tags file and then invoke C omni-completion. notes.text: A flaw was found in FFmpeg. A remote attacker can exploit an infinite loop vulnerability in the RTP/ASF demuxer by sending a specially crafted stream. This vulnerability occurs because the rtp_asf_fix_header function does not properly validate the size of data chunks, preventing the processing loop from advancing. Successful exploitation leads to CPU exhaustion, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: FFmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted RTP/ASF stream
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The impact rating reflects that this issue strictly impacts Availability (A:H) with low/no effect on Confidentiality or Integrity. Exploitation requires an active application to ingest and demux a maliciously crafted RTP/ASF media stream; passive files at rest pose no risk. 

Successful exploitation results in high CPU consumption that stalls the stream-processing thread or container worker, but it does not cause memory corruption or allow arbitrary code execution. Systems that do not dynamically ingest untrusted, real-time RTP/ASF network streams are effectively out of scope for operational disruption.
